doc.title: Alan Raph interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001

title: Which dates were hard: rhythm, tempo and reading
summary: Raph says he was mostly bored but sometimes scared by difficult dates. Tempo, rhythm and accurate reading were the challenges.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Isn’t that curious because you’ve said that you had gotten to a point where not too much scared you or made you nervous.

Well, I know, most of the time I was bored to death but occasionally I was scared to death you know. And it goes from one extreme to the other. There’s no middle ground. Most of the time you just kind of do it. But then every now and then something comes up and you think uh oh, I’m over my head, I will not make this.
Is it mostly rhythmic stuff? Or is it hard to pin it down?

Rhythmic, tempo, accuracy were the considerations. Make sure that the tempo fits. Make sure that everything is gelling feel-wise, where the tempo comes into it and hitting right at the right moment. And then rhythms because a whole big thing because you don’t have a lot of time to learn the arrangement. If you’re playing with a band that plays it every night, after a week or so you know it. But having it on a recording, seeing it for the first time, the second and third time you’re really intent on making sure that you’re reading © Fillius Jazz Archive -15-

exactly what’s written. Because it’s easy to confuse a figure with something else. It’s easy to poke in a note. And those are some of the considerations. Technically — there were some technical things too.
